baseline.name: Copy the supplied balances during construction
baseline.approach: Allocate an owned n-element balance array and copy initial values; use direct indexing for later operations.

archived.name: Borrow the caller's balance array
archived.time: O(1) construction, deposit, withdraw and transfer
archived.space: O(1) auxiliary object; the caller's existing n-element balance array is borrowed

why: Borrowing avoids the constructor copy and duplicate balance storage while keeping the same direct-index operations.
quantitative_comparison: The copy baseline reads/writes n balance values into a new array. This source copies zero balance elements and allocates only its small object; deposit/withdraw/transfer have the same constant-growth work. This compares construction/storage, not transaction throughput.
tradeoffs: Caller storage must remain alive and can be changed externally. The source does not provide isolation, negative-amount validation or general arithmetic/concurrency safety.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
